label: DAY 12
title: I let a bot learn my game from zero. After 10,000 games it beat every bot I wrote.

scenes.title: 10,000 games of practice
scenes.caption: learner
lines: Nobody told this bot the rules. It started knowing nothing. After ten thousand practice games, it catches fifty one coins a game, and it never hits a bomb.

scenes.title: My game: Sky Catch

items.text: Move left, stay, or move right

lines: I coded a little game. Coins and bombs fall down five lanes. Catch coins, avoid bombs, two hundred ticks a game.

scenes.title: My coin chaser
scenes.caption: chases coins only
lines: First I wrote bots by hand. This one runs at the nearest coin. It never looks for bombs, so it lasts about thirty four ticks.

scenes.title: Bots I wrote: coins per game
lines: My best one just dodges. It stands still and steps aside when a bomb is coming. Sixteen coins a game, and it never dies.

scenes.title: After 10 games
scenes.caption: learner: 10 games
lines: Then the learner. It gets plus one for a coin and minus ten for a bomb, and nothing else. After ten games, it still walks into bombs.

scenes.title: Learner: coins per game
lines: After a hundred games, twenty three coins. That already beats every bot I wrote.
After a thousand, forty three. At ten thousand, fifty one. A hundred thousand games didn't help: forty eight.

scenes.title: What it can see
log: only a 3 x 3 patch above its head
1 score per move in each one
lines: It only sees a three by three patch above its head.
In ten thousand games it met five hundred ninety different patches, and learned a score for each move in each one. That's called Q learning.
It caught sixty one percent of every coin that fell.

scenes.text: My best rule: 16 coins. Its practice: 51.
scenes.sub: what game should it learn next?
lines: My best hand written rule got sixteen. Practice got fifty one. What game should it learn next? Tell me in the comments.
